backlog.spec: Replace construct_packing with a multi-start optimizer: variables are (x,y,r) for 26 circles; maximize sum r using scipy.optimize.minimize SLSQP with vectorized inequality constraints (pairwise dist - ri - rj >= 0, borders r<=x<=1-r, etc.) and analytic jacobians. Use fixed seed, random uniform centers, r0=0.05, run until ~200s elapsed, keep best. Finally shrink radii by 1e-12 and verify validity.
backlog.title: SLSQP joint optimization from random starts

backlog.spec: After any center layout, compute optimal radii by scipy.optimize.linprog (maximize sum r s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=border distance, r>=0). Use this instead of the greedy compute_max_radii. Then alternate with a small SLSQP step on centers. Shrink by 1e-12 at end.
backlog.title: LP radii refinement given centers

backlog.spec: Initialize centers from a perturbed hexagonal lattice (rows of 5,5,5,5,6 or 5,6,5,6,4 variants, scaled into the square), random jitter with fixed seed, and polish with SLSQP on (x,y,r). Try several row patterns and keep the best.
backlog.title: Hex-grid initialization with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Starting from the best SLSQP solution, do basin hopping: perturb 1-3 random circles (relocate smallest circle to random position or jitter all by sigma 0.03), re-solve with SLSQP, accept if improved (or Metropolis with small temperature). Loop within a 200s time budget.
backlog.title: Basin hopping on centers

backlog.spec: Stage 1: minimize -sum r + mu*sum(overlap^2 + border violation^2) with L-BFGS-B over (x,y,r), increasing mu over 6 stages (1e1..1e5). Stage 2: SLSQP with hard constraints. Use many random starts with fixed seed.
backlog.title: Penalty-method gradient descent warm start

backlog.spec: Initialize with larger radii (0.12) near the center and smaller (0.06) near edges, with 4 corner circles placed at corners with r~0.1. Centers by jittered grid. Run SLSQP from this start with several seeds.
backlog.title: Radii-size-biased initialization

backlog.spec: Fix initial positions of 4 corner circles and ~8 edge circles along the borders, fill interior with random points; optimize all variables with SLSQP. Multi-start over interior randomness.
backlog.title: Corner and edge seeded layout

backlog.spec: After best candidate found, rerun SLSQP with ftol=1e-15, maxiter=2000 from it, then project to feasibility by LP radii and shrink by 1e-13. Aims to squeeze the last 1e-6.
backlog.title: Fine-tune with tighter SLSQP tolerances

backlog.spec: Use scipy trust-constr with sparse jacobian constraints for the (x,y,r) problem from the best SLSQP solution, to compare convergence quality; keep whichever is better after feasibility repair.
backlog.title: Trust-constr alternative solver

backlog.spec: For speed, include only pair constraints for pairs with distance < 0.4 in the current iterate, re-solving with SLSQP in an outer loop that rebuilds the pair list and checks for violations. Allows many more restarts within time.
backlog.title: Active-set neighbor-only constraints

backlog.spec: Run a Monte Carlo move scheme on centers with LP-computed radii as objective (fast numpy), temperature decaying from 0.01 to 1e-5, then finish with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Simulated annealing on radii-weighted energy

backlog.spec: Iterate: from the current best packing, remove the circle with smallest radius, find the largest empty hole via sampled grid points maximizing clearance, reinsert it there, and re-optimize with SLSQP. Repeat while improving.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert smallest circle

backlog.spec: Initialize with 1 center + rings (e.g., 1+6+12+7 or 4 corners + ring structures), rotated by random angles, then SLSQP. Search over ring counts partitions summing to 26.
backlog.title: Swap-based perturbation of ring structure

backlog.spec: Optimize with a constraint scaling: first maximize sum r with radii capped at 0.08, then 0.10, then 0.12, then uncapped, warm starting SLSQP each stage, to avoid bad local minima.
backlog.title: Staged radius growth

backlog.spec: Generate random points, apply 20 iterations of Lloyd relaxation in the unit square (via sampled grid approximation), use as centers, with radii set to half nearest-neighbor distance, then SLSQP.
backlog.title: Lloyd/Voronoi-based initialization

backlog.spec: Impose a mirror (diagonal) or 180° rotational symmetry: optimize 13 free circles plus their images (or with some on the axis), reducing dimension; then release symmetry and polish with full SLSQP.
backlog.title: Symmetric packing search

backlog.spec: Use scipy differential_evolution over centers with LP-based radii fitness for a coarse search (seeded, small popsize, limited maxiter), then SLSQP polish of the best.
backlog.title: Differential evolution on low-dim parametrization

backlog.spec: Keep the global best solution; each restart add Gaussian noise with sigma sampled log-uniformly in [0.005,0.08] to centers, set radii to 0.8x, resolve with SLSQP. Adopt improvements.
backlog.title: Perturb-best restarts with decaying sigma

backlog.spec: Use L-BFGS on a smooth objective sum r minus barrier terms -t*sum log(slack) with t decreasing from 1e-2 to 1e-8 (interior point style) from feasible start, then SLSQP final polish.
backlog.title: Soft-min objective annealing

backlog.spec: Provide analytic jac for constraints and objective using numpy index arrays of all 325 pairs, making SLSQP ~10x faster so more restarts fit in the 4-min budget. Use time checks to stop at 220s.
backlog.title: Vectorized analytic Jacobians

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, identify active constraints (slack<1e-9), then solve the nonlinear system of equalities via Newton/least_squares to machine precision for the active contact graph, increasing accuracy; finally shrink by 1e-14.
backlog.title: Tangent-graph rigidity refinement

backlog.spec: Seed with a known-style structure: 4 large corner circles r~0.13, mid-edge medium circles, and a small-circle interior filling gaps, randomized sizes per seed; run SLSQP and keep best across seeds.
backlog.title: Different circle count mix seeding

backlog.spec: Maintain 8 candidate packings; each round, perturb each with different sigma, SLSQP re-solve briefly (maxiter 60), swap worst with best periodically. Run within time limit, finish with full SLSQP on best.
backlog.title: Parallel-tempering style population

backlog.spec: Generate initial centers from a sheared/rotated lattice with random angle and spacing chosen to yield ~26 points inside the square (trim or add random points), then SLSQP. Many seeds.
backlog.title: Random lattice-shear initializations

backlog.spec: Allow SLSQP to finish with small violations (~1e-10), then repair exactly: compute radii by LP with constraint d_ij - 1e-12 and border margins, ensuring zero-tolerance validity while losing at most 1e-11 sum.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant relaxed final repair

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty/constraint forcing r_i >= 0.03 in early restarts to prevent degenerate tiny circles, then relax to r>=0 for final polish. Compare local minima quality across seeds.
backlog.title: Radius lower bound regularization

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, add a move that swaps the centers of a large circle and a neighboring small circle (radii re-initialized to the swapped ones), then SLSQP re-solves. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Move-set: swap neighbors of different size

backlog.spec: Rescale variables so that SLSQP is better conditioned: optimize in units where radii are multiplied by 10, with constraints normalized; check whether convergence reaches better optima across 50 seeds.
backlog.title: Constraint-scaled variables

backlog.spec: Phase 1: 300 quick SLSQP runs with maxiter=40 from random starts; Phase 2: take top 10 and run full convergence with maxiter=1000; Phase 3: basin hopping on the top 3. Time-budgeted to 220s.
backlog.title: Two-phase coarse-then-fine multistart

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, do pattern search: for each circle try moving center by ±delta in 8 directions (delta halving from 0.01 to 1e-8), recompute LP radii, accept if sum increases. Final feasibility shrink.
backlog.title: Gradient-free coordinate refinement

backlog.spec: In construct_packing, add a phase that searches symmetric packings. Pick a random symmetry: reflection about the diagonal x=y, or about x=0.5. Generate 13 free circles plus mirrored copies, or k free circles plus m circles on the axis, so that the total is 26. Run the staged SLSQP on the full 26-circle problem from this symmetric start, with no symmetry enforced. Spend about 40 seconds on this phase, then compare the results with the random-start phase and keep the best.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric search

backlog.spec: After the multistart phase, spend the remaining time on a loop. Take the best packing, choose a random center point and the 4-6 circles nearest to it, and re-randomize their centers inside a disc around that point. Set their radii to 0.03 and set the other radii to 0.9 of their current values. Run the staged SLSQP and then the LP. Accept the result only if it improves on the best. The perturbation is local, unlike the earlier global perturbations.
backlog.title: Perturb incumbent by shrinking a random cluster

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, re-run SLSQP from it with ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=1000. Use only the near-active constraints (pairs with gap < 0.02) for speed. Then run the LP radii step with a shrink of 1e-12 instead of 1e-7, followed by the existing violation-repair loop. The goal is to recover about 2.6e-6 of the sum from the safety margin. Verify validity in double precision with an explicit check, and fall back to the 1e-9 margin if any violation remains.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish with trust-constr or tight SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random starts with starts whose sizes come from a prescribed distribution. Draw 4 radii from U(0.12,0.16), 8 from U(0.08,0.11) and 14 from U(0.04,0.08), and sort them. Place circles greedily, largest first, at random positions using rejection sampling for non-overlap against the square and the previous circles, relaxing if needed. Feed them to the staged SLSQP with r0 set to these radii times 0.8. Use about half the time budget on these starts and half on uniform starts.
backlog.title: Radius-distribution-biased starts

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, relax each random start with L-BFGS on an energy. The energy is the sum over pairs of max(0, r_i+r_j-d)^2 plus the sum of wall violations squared, with radii fixed at a random target sizes vector with mean 0.1. Run this for 100 iterations with an analytic gradient. This spreads the centers out and gives SLSQP a much better-conditioned start. Use random target radii each start.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion energy pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Run many more starts per unit time. For each start, run only one short SLSQP stage (cap 0.12, maxiter 60) and compute the LP sum. Keep the top 10% of starts by LP sum, and give them the full staged SLSQP with maxiter 500. Use a fixed seed and a time-based cutoff at 200 s total, split 50/50 between screening and full polishing.
backlog.title: Cheap screening of many starts

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing. Repeat: remove the 2 smallest circles, or 2 random circles. Find the largest empty spots by evaluating a 100x100 grid of points and computing the distance to the nearest circle edge and walls. Place the 2 circles at the two best well-separated holes with a radius equal to half the clearance. Run SLSQP at the capped 0.12 and uncapped stages, then the LP. Accept only if improved. Differ from the earlier single reinsert by using pairs and random choices.
backlog.title: Remove-two-and-reinsert at largest holes

backlog.spec: Add a regularization stage for the early part of each SLSQP start. Maximize sum(r) + lam * sum over pairs of exp(-gap_ij / 0.01), with lam=1e-3 decayed to 0 over the 4 stages. This rewards near contact and helps rigid networks form. The final stage uses the original objective. Keep the full constraints.
backlog.title: Radius-sum objective with smooth penalty on contact count

backlog.spec: Use a bilevel scheme: the outer variables are the 52 center coordinates, and the objective is the LP-optimal sum of radii for those centers. Run Nelder-Mead-free random local search: perturb the centers of 1-3 circles by N(0,sigma) with sigma decaying from 0.05 to 0.002, compute the LP value, and accept if it improves. Apply it to the top 5 packings from the multistart for about 60 s, then finish with SLSQP polish. The LP gives an exact radii response, so this gives an independent move type.
backlog.title: Centers-only optimization via LP inner solve

backlog.spec: Fix a structure on the starts: circles 0-3 at the corners with radius about 0.13 and 8 edge circles spaced along the sides with radii about 0.09, as in the old _seed function but with the 14 interior circles drawn from a jittered 4x4 grid with 2 points dropped at random. Use 30% of the starts like this, with the rest uniform. Run the same staged SLSQP, which lets the corners move. This mixes in the known structure of good packings.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored templates with random interior

backlog.spec: Change the RNG seed in construct_packing to a seed derived from a list of several values (e.g. loop over seeds 1..8 each getting an equal share of the 200s budget via per-seed time slices), keeping staged SLSQP and full pair constraints. Keep the global best. The goal is simply to sample different basins than seed 12345 did; the LP radii polish stays as is.
backlog.title: Incumbent-seeded multi-seed restart with new RNG streams

backlog.spec: During the multistart loop keep the top 5 distinct results by sum of radii. After the loop, for each, run a final SLSQP with ftol=1e-15, maxiter=1000 and no radius cap from the stored (x,y,r), followed by _lp_radii, and return the best. This captures the last 1e-6 to 1e-4 that the 300-iteration stages leave unconverged.
backlog.title: Basin polish of top-K candidates

backlog.spec: After multistart, take the best centers and run scipy minimize (method Powell, maxiter ~ 2000, time-limited to 30s) on the objective -sum(_lp_radii(centers)) (without the 1e-7 shrink inside the search). The LP gives exact radii for each center set so this explores nonsmooth contact-graph changes that SLSQP cannot. Finish with the shrink for validity.
backlog.title: Centers-only LP-inner optimisation with Nelder-Mead/Powell on best

backlog.spec: Add a start mode where 13 circles are free and the other 13 are their reflection across the diagonal x=y (or, variant, 6 pairs plus 14 on the axis... keep it simple: 13 free plus mirror with a few points on the diagonal allowed to be self-paired). Run SLSQP on the reduced variables (x,y,r for 13 circles, mirror derived) for staged growth, then release the symmetry and re-optimize fully with the 4-stage SLSQP. Use half the time budget for symmetric starts and half for plain random.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric constrained search

backlog.spec: Initialize r0 per circle from a lognormal or mix: 4 circles r0 ~0.12, 8 at ~0.09, 14 at ~0.04, assigned to random positions, with centers drawn uniformly. Previous graded starts also fixed positions; this one only randomizes sizes while keeping uniform positions, and caps staged radii at 0.08/0.10/0.12/None as before. Alternate with plain starts.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted random starts with heavy-tailed size distribution

backlog.spec: For each start run only the first stage (cap 0.08, maxiter 60) and compute sum from the LP radii. Collect batches of 50 starts, keep the top 10 by the screening score, and run the full remaining staged schedule only on those. This lets the budget cover roughly 3-5x more starts.
backlog.title: Cheap screening: short SLSQP then continue only top 20%

backlog.spec: Before staged SLSQP, run L-BFGS-B on E = -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 + border violation^2) with mu rising 10, 100, 1000, 1e4 over about 4 rounds from random starts. The pass lets circles pass through each other and reorder while radii are soft, then hand the result to SLSQP with a 1e-3 shrink of the radii. The difference from the earlier penalty warm start is the larger mu schedule and the final shrink.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant penalty annealing before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Fix start positions so that 4 circles sit at the corners with r0=0.13 (centers at r0 from both walls), 12 more around the edges at random positions along the perimeter with r0 0.08, and the remaining 10 are uniform random in [0.2,0.8]. SLSQP then runs free (no fixing). Randomize the edge circle parameter t each start. Run for half the budget alongside the uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored templates with random interior

backlog.spec: For the best result, identify the active contacts (pairs with gap <1e-6, walls with gap <1e-6), then solve the nonlinear system of equalities for those contacts with scipy.optimize.root or least_squares (unknowns x,y,r), starting from the best solution, to reach machine-precision tangency. Then check that all constraints hold, shrink by 1e-12 relative to r, and return if the sum improves, otherwise fall back to the LP result.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish with active-set KKT solve

backlog.spec: In construct_packing keep a list of the top 5 (by LP-radii sum) results from the multistart loop, stopping the loop at 150s. In the remaining time, for each of them run SLSQP again from the LP-refined radii and centers with maxiter 1000, ftol 1e-15, no radius cap, then recompute _lp_radii. Keep the best result. Always return a valid fallback if polish yields a worse or non-finite result.
backlog.title: Basin polish of top-K candidates

backlog.spec: Add a second multistart family in which circles are constrained to be symmetric about the diagonal x=y. Use 4 diagonal circles (x=y, free t) and 11 mirrored pairs (13 free points total gives 26 only if diag count is even; use 4 diagonal + 11 pairs). Parametrize z with the reduced variables, build full x,y,r vectors, and reuse the existing constraint functions via a chain-rule wrapper or simply start SLSQP from a symmetrized random start and then release the symmetry for the staged full SLSQP. Run 40% of the time budget on symmetric starts, the rest on the existing random starts. Take the best LP-validated result.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric constrained search

backlog.spec: After the multistart phase, take the best packing. Repeat for about 60 seconds: pick 2 circles at random (biased to the smallest radii), delete them, find the two largest empty holes by evaluating a 100x100 grid of points for distance to nearest circle edge and walls (pick the best grid point, mark it filled with a small radius, then the next), place the circles there with radius 0.03, run the staged _optimize and _lp_radii, accept if the sum improves.
backlog.title: Remove-two-and-reinsert at largest holes

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP start, relax random centers with 50 L-BFGS-B iterations on a Riesz-like energy sum 1/(d_ij^2+eps) plus wall repulsion 1/(x^2)+1/((1-x)^2) (and the same in y, with clipping to avoid blowups) so that points start well spread but not on a lattice. Then use random per-circle radii r0 from uniform(0.02,0.1) and run the usual staged SLSQP. Use this for half of the starts, alternating with the existing uniform starts.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion energy pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: Starts that fix the structure of the best-known type packings: put 4 circles near the corners at (0.1,0.1)-style positions with radius 0.12 plus jitter, 8 circles along the edges at random positions with radius 0.08, and 14 interior uniformly random points with radius 0.05 (no hand coordinates beyond this template). Use it for 50% of starts interleaved with the existing uniform starts, running the existing staged SLSQP. Only the start generator changes.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored templates with random interior

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best centers and run scipy minimize with method Powell on the 52 center coordinates, objective -sum(_lp_radii(x,y)) (return 0 if LP fails), xtol 1e-9, maxfev bounded by a 60s time guard raising an exception when exceeded (catch it and keep the best seen so far). Accept only if the final LP sum beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Centers-only Powell with LP inner solve

backlog.spec: Replace the first SLSQP stage with an L-BFGS-B penalty stage: minimize -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0,overlap)^2) over (x,y,r) with analytic gradients, with mu annealed 10, 100, 1000, 1e4 (about 100 iterations each) from random starts, then continue with the staged SLSQP caps. This lets circles pass through each other early and explores topologies.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant penalty annealing

backlog.spec: Run 300 random starts through only the cap-0.08 and cap-0.10 SLSQP stages with maxiter 100, record the sum of radii, then fully finish (cap 0.12 and uncapped, maxiter 500) only the top 20% by partial sum. Budget total 200s with a time guard. Use a new RNG seed (e.g. 777) so different basins are visited.
backlog.title: Cheap screening then continue top 20%

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii from a lognormal (sigma 0.5, median 0.06) clipped to [0.02,0.18] and centers uniformly from [0.05,0.95], with the larger circles placed nearer the square corners by sorting radii and assigning the largest 4 to the corners with jitter 0.05. Use RNG seed 2024 and run the existing staged SLSQP on every start until 200s.
backlog.title: Radius-distribution-biased heavy-tail starts with new seed

backlog.spec: Add a final stage: after the best result is chosen, drop the 1e-7 shrink margin in LP to 1e-12 and then verify validity in double precision with an exact check (pair distances minus radius sums, walls); if any violation, subtract the maximal violation from the involved radii only. This recovers about 2.5e-6 of sum. Also try the LP on center-perturbed variants: 20 random perturbations of 1e-4 of the centers followed by LP, keeping the best valid.
backlog.title: Tiny-radius shrink regularization and two-stage polish

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing and do a time-capped (60s) loop: pick a random circle, move its center to a random point in the largest empty region (sample 2000 random points, choose the one maximizing distance to nearest circle edge), set its radius small, and also jitter 3 neighbouring centers with sigma 0.03. Run the staged SLSQP (caps 0.12, None) from this start, then LP radii. Accept if the sum improves (or with Metropolis acceptance at T=0.002). Keep the best valid packing. Use a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Contact-graph basin hopping with LP inner

backlog.spec: Change the construct_packing RNG seed from 12345 to a loop of 6 different seeds (e.g. 1,7,42,2024,31337,999), each getting about 30s of multistart time. Keep the global best over all seeds. Keep the staged radius cap schedule and the final polish unchanged. This explores different basins than the stuck one.
backlog.title: Different base seeds with time split

backlog.spec: Replace the radius cap schedule (0.08, 0.10, 0.12, None) with a finer one: (0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.09, 0.10, 0.11, 0.12, 0.14, None), with maxiter 150 per stage. Everything else stays the same. Slow growth lets the circles rearrange gradually, which may find better basins.
backlog.title: Finer cap schedule with more stages

backlog.spec: Generate starts with prescribed size classes: 4 corner circles near (0.12,0.12) with r0 0.12, 4 circles with r0 0.10 at random interior spots, 8 circles with r0 0.08 near the edges, and 10 circles with r0 0.04 random. Use jitter of 0.03 on positions. Use this for half of the multistart runs, alternating with the uniform random starts. Run the staged SLSQP as is.
backlog.title: Size-ordered ladder start

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing and repeat for 60s: delete the 2 circles with the smallest radii (or random 2 of the 6 smallest), find the 2 largest holes by sampling 5000 random points and picking points with the largest clearance (the second one at least 0.1 from the first), reinsert the circles there with radius = 0.5 * clearance, and run the staged SLSQP from that state. Keep the result if the LP sum is better.
backlog.title: Remove two smallest and reinsert at holes

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP run, relax the random start with 200 steps of gradient descent on the energy sum over pairs of max(0, 2*0.09 - d)^2 plus the wall terms max(0, 0.09 - x)^2 etc., with the points clipped to [0.03,0.97]. Use vectorized numpy and a step size of 0.1. This spreads the points evenly like a Poisson-disk sample. Then start SLSQP with r0 = 0.05. Use it in all multistart runs.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion energy pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: After the existing SLSQP polish, run scipy minimize with method trust-constr on the best packing, with the full vectorized constraints and Jacobian (NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0, upper bound inf, jac=_cons_jac), gtol 1e-12, maxiter 500, and a 30s time cap through a callback. Then rebuild the radii with the LP and a shrink of 1e-12. Only accept the result if _valid holds and the sum is larger.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish

backlog.spec: For the early stages of SLSQP (the caps 0.08 and 0.10), replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(r) + lam * sum((r - rbar)^2), where lam = 0.5 and rbar is the mean radius. This favours uniform radii first. Then use the true objective in the 0.12 and uncapped stages. Give the analytic gradient. This changes the early landscape and gives new basins.
backlog.title: Objective with power-mean annealing of radii

backlog.spec: Build the starts from a hexagonal-style layout of 5 rows with row counts drawn at random from permutations of (5,5,5,5,6) and (4,5,6,5,6), with uneven spacing, then add Gaussian noise with sigma 0.04 to the centers and multiply the radii by a random factor. Remove or add random circles to reach exactly 26. Use r0 = 0.06. Run 30% of the multistart runs this way, with the staged SLSQP.
backlog.title: Structured hybrid: hex rows with 5-6 split plus perturbation

backlog.spec: Run 600 random starts through the capped stage 0.10 only (maxiter 100), compute the LP sum for each, and keep the top 25. Then run the full staged schedule (caps 0.12 and None, maxiter 300) on the top 25 only. Choose the best. Use the time budget of 200s total, and stop the screening at 90s. This allows far more starts to be explored than the full pipeline per start.
backlog.title: Screen-then-finish batch with large pool

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing and do a time-capped (60s) loop: pick a random circle, relocate it to a random point (or swap two circles of different radii), then run one SLSQP pass (full pair constraints, maxiter 150, starting radii from the LP on the new centers shrunk by 0.7) and finally _lp_radii. Accept only if the LP sum improves. Keep a fixed seed. This explores neighbouring contact graphs rather than random restarts.
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation with LP inner solve

backlog.spec: Replace the single default_rng(12345) with four independent rngs (seeds 1, 7, 99, 2024), each given a 50s budget in round-robin order, keeping the global best by LP sum. Everything else (staged SLSQP, polish) is unchanged. The aim is to escape the basin that seed 12345 lands in.
backlog.title: Different base seed with time split across 4 seeds

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that builds rows of circles with counts such as 5,6,5,6,4 or 6,5,6,5,4 (random permutation of row counts summing to 26), evenly spaced in y, with x offsets staggered, plus Gaussian jitter of 0.02 and initial radii 0.05. Use it for half of the multistart runs, alternating with uniform random starts. Run the staged SLSQP as usual.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts with 5-6 split

backlog.spec: Before each final SLSQP stage, run an extra stage that maximises sum(r^p) with p = 0.5 first, then p = 0.8, then p = 1. This is the same constraints, with warm starts, and uses analytic gradients p*r^(p-1) (with r clipped to at least 1e-6). The concave objective spreads the radii evenly and can change which contact graph the solver ends in. Use it in the staged growth loop in _optimize.
backlog.title: Power-mean objective annealing

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP re-polish, identify active constraints (gap < 1e-6). Solve the KKT equality system for these constraints, taking the active pair and border distances as equalities, with scipy.optimize.fsolve or least_squares on the unknowns (x, y, r), starting from the current solution. If the solution is feasible and its sum is larger than the current one, use it, then shrink by 1e-12. This gets the sum to machine precision.
backlog.title: Trust-constr final polish with active set

backlog.spec: Run 400 random starts with only the cap 0.08 SLSQP stage (maxiter 100), and rank them by sum of radii. Then finish only the top 10 through the remaining stages (0.10, 0.12, uncapped) with full maxiter. Keep time split about 60s screening and 140s finishing. Seed 777 for a fresh basin sample.
backlog.title: Large pool screen then finish top 10

backlog.spec: Generate starts where 4 circles are put near the corners (at 0.1 from each corner, with jitter 0.03) with r0 in 0.10 to 0.15, and the other 22 centers are uniform random in the square with lognormal radii (median 0.05, sigma 0.5) clipped to 0.15. Use seed 2025. Run staged SLSQP and LP as usual.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed size starts with corner bias

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in each start, run 200 L-BFGS-B iterations on the energy sum over pairs of max(0, ri+rj-d)^2 plus border violations, where the radii are fixed random samples from a size distribution (uniform 0.04-0.12 sorted to be larger in the center). Then run staged SLSQP with the relaxed centers and the radii initialised to 0.5 of those fixed values. This gives packings with a designed size gradient.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion pre-relaxation with varying radii

backlog.spec: Use the variable r scaled by 10 (z_r = 10 r) and the pair constraints in the form sqrt(dx²+dy²) - ri - rj >= 0 with the analytic Jacobian (dx/d, dy/d, -1, -1). The better-conditioned constraints may change which local optimum SLSQP reaches and speed it up so that more starts fit in the time budget. Keep the time limit at 200s.
backlog.title: Constraint scaling and SLSQP on variable subsets

backlog.spec: Keep the top 8 distinct multistart packings (by sum). For each, spend about 15s of repeated attempts: jitter all the centers with Gaussian noise of sigma 0.01 to 0.03 and set radii to 0.8 of the LP radii, then run the SLSQP with full constraints, followed by the LP. Keep the improvements. Finally, take the global best and re-polish it.
backlog.title: Basin polish of top-K with random jitter

backlog.spec: Add a start generator in construct_packing used for about half the multistart iterations. Pick a random row-count pattern (e.g. 5,5,5,5,6 / 5,6,5,6,4 / 6,5,6,5,4 summing to 26), place the circles in evenly spaced rows with x offsets alternating per row, add Gaussian jitter of sigma 0.02, and set r0=0.05. Feed this into the existing _optimize pipeline unchanged, keep full pair constraints and keep the LP radii step. Use a new rng stream (seed 777) so it does not disturb the current uniform starts. Keep the 200s time budget.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts 5-6 split

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, run scipy minimize with method Powell on the 52 center coordinates of the best packing. The objective is -sum(_lp_radii(x,y,0)) and returns 0 on LP failure. Use a hard wall-clock guard of 50s through a callback that raises StopIteration, and wrap everything in try/except. Accept the result only if the LP sum improves. Then run the existing SLSQP polish and the final shrink. Reduce the multistart time limit to 140s to make room.
backlog.title: Centers-only Powell with LP inner on best

backlog.spec: Replace the single rng seed 12345 with 4 sequential seeds (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4), each given 45s of the multistart loop, with the global best kept across seeds. The existing 200s total stays the same. The goal is to escape the one basin that seed 12345 repeatedly finds. Make sure at least one start completes per seed.
backlog.title: Different base seeds with time split

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing. For 40 trials, remove the 2 circles with the smallest radii (or 2 random ones from the 6 smallest on later trials). Sample 20000 random points and place the two circles at the points with the largest clearance from the remaining circles and the borders, enforcing that the two do not coincide. Set their initial radii to 0.02, run _optimize with the capped stages (cap None only), and score with the LP. Keep the best. Stop at 60s total.
backlog.title: Remove two smallest and reinsert at holes

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for alternate multistart iterations. It draws r0 from a lognormal (mean log 0.06, sigma 0.5) clipped to [0.02, 0.18]. Four of the circles with the largest r0 are placed near the corners (0.1 to 0.2 from each corner with jitter). The rest are uniform in [0.05, 0.95]. Use a new rng seed (2024) for these starts. Run them through _optimize unchanged.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed size starts with corner bias

backlog.spec: Phase 1 (80s): generate random starts and run only the first two capped stages (cap 0.08 and 0.10, maxiter 100) for each. Record the LP-scored sum for each result. Phase 2: take the top 10 by that score and run the remaining stages (0.12, None) from their phase-1 states. Phase 3: pick the best and polish as now. This should allow about 3x more starts explored than the full pipeline per start.
backlog.title: Screen large pool then finish top 10

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP run, draw r0 uniform in [0.03, 0.12] and run 150 iterations of L-BFGS-B on the energy sum over pairs of max(0, r_i+r_j+0.005-d)^2 plus border penalties of max(0, r_i-x)^2 etc., with analytic gradient, over centers only. Use the relaxed centers and the same r0 as the SLSQP start. Apply this only on every third multistart iteration, so the other starts keep the current behaviour.
backlog.title: Soft-repulsion pre-relaxation with varying radii

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, run a loop up to 60s. Each iteration takes the best packing, picks a random pair of touching circles with a radius ratio above 1.3, swaps their centers, and also jitters all the centers by sigma 0.01. Re-run _optimize with r0 set to 0.7 times the current radii, using only the final uncapped stage, then LP radii. Accept if improved over the best. Seed the rng with 99.
backlog.title: Perturb best by swapping large and small neighbors

backlog.spec: Create structured starts where k circles (k random in 14 to 18) are placed on the square perimeter ring at inset 0.07 with equal spacing, with a random phase and a jitter of 0.01. The remaining 26-k circles go on an inner ring or random interior positions in [0.2, 0.8]. Set the perimeter r0 to 0.09 and the interior r0 to 0.07. Use it for one third of the multistart iterations with a separate rng (seed 31337), through the unchanged _optimize.
backlog.title: Border-tangent circle count seeding

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that builds 5 rows of centers with counts like 5,5,6,5,5 or 6,5,5,5,5 (sum 26), evenly spaced in y in [0.1,0.9] and x spaced in [0.1,0.9] with alternate rows offset by half spacing, plus Gaussian jitter sigma 0.02, initial radii 0.05. Run the existing staged _optimize and LP on each. Use about 30% of the time budget on these starts with several random row-count permutations and jitter seeds (own rng seed 777), and keep the best overall packing with the existing multistart result.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts 5-6 split with SLSQP

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, identify active constraints (gap < 1e-7) and solve the nonlinear system of active equalities (pair distance = r_i+r_j, border tangencies) plus KKT stationarity for sum(r) using least-squares Newton (scipy.optimize.least_squares) with multipliers as unknowns. Accept only if the result passes _valid after a 1e-12 shrink and has a larger sum than the SLSQP result.
backlog.title: Trust-constr / active-set KKT Newton final polish

backlog.spec: Replace the single rng seed 12345 with four seeds (e.g. 1, 2024, 31337, 987654), each given 50s of the multistart loop with uniform starts. Keep the global best by LP-scored sum. This tests whether a different basin beats -2.6360.
backlog.title: New base seeds with 4-way time split

backlog.spec: From the best packing, remove the two smallest circles, find the two largest empty holes by sampling a 200x200 grid of points and computing the distance-to-nearest-circle-edge (placing the second after the first), place new centers there with r=0.03, and run the staged _optimize. Repeat over the combinations of the 3 smallest circles removed and the top 5 holes, accepting improvements, within 60s.
backlog.title: Remove two smallest and reinsert at largest holes

backlog.spec: New start generator: 4 circles near corners at (0.12±0.03) with r0 drawn lognormal around 0.12, the other 22 centers uniform random with r0 lognormal (median 0.07, sigma 0.4) clipped to [0.02, 0.2]. Use in alternation with the uniform starts, with a different rng seed (2027). Keep the staged SLSQP.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed size starts with corner bias

backlog.spec: Generate 400 uniform random starts and run only the first SLSQP stage (cap 0.08, maxiter 100) on each, cheaply. Rank them by the sum of radii after that stage, then run the full remaining staged schedule only on the top 10, followed by LP radii. Spend the leftover time on the standard multistart loop.
backlog.title: Large pool screen then finish top 10

backlog.spec: Take the best packing and its contact graph. Repeatedly pick a random circle and its neighbors, move their centers by gaussian sigma 0.03 and re-solve the radii by _lp_radii, then run the polish SLSQP for 100 iterations only if the LP sum is within 0.03 of the best. Accept improvements, within a 60s budget (seed 5).
backlog.title: Contact-graph perturbation with LP inner solve

backlog.spec: For the best packing, run a loop with penalty weight mu in (10, 100, 1000, 1e4): minimize -sum(r) + mu*sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + border violations^2) with L-BFGS-B using analytic gradients, starting from the best, with small random center jitter at the start of each of 20 repeats. Then finish with SLSQP and the LP, and accept only if valid and better.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant penalty annealing as last stage

backlog.spec: Search over packings symmetric about the diagonal x=y: 4 circles on the diagonal and 11 mirrored pairs (parameters: 4 diagonal t, 11 centers, radii). Optimize via SLSQP in the reduced variable space (about 37 variables), with full pair constraints computed by expanding to 26 circles. Use 40s of random starts, then take the best as an initial point for the full unconstrained _optimize and polish.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric constrained search

backlog.spec: In each multistart iteration, sample the radius cap schedule randomly: a sorted tuple of 2-4 caps drawn uniformly from [0.06, 0.16] plus a final None, and a random maxiter in {150, 300}. This diversifies the basin each start falls into. Use seed-based rng for repeatability and keep the best by LP sum.
backlog.title: Randomized cap schedules per restart

backlog.spec: In construct_packing's final stage, the LP shrink is 1e-12 or 1e-9 and the earlier LP uses 1e-7. Replace the final selection with a loop over shrinks (1e-15, 1e-14, 1e-13, 1e-12, 1e-11, 1e-10) and take the first one where _valid passes and the sum is largest. Also, instead of subtracting a uniform shrink, compute radii with LP and then reduce only the radii of circles involved in violated pairs by the exact violation amount. This recovers up to ~1e-7 of sum. Keep the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Measure and shrink the safety margin

backlog.spec: Change default_rng(12345) to a different seed (e.g. 2024) and keep everything else identical. The incumbent may be a lucky basin for seed 12345, and a new seed gives a fresh sample of local optima from the same successful pipeline. Make it a single constant at the top of construct_packing.
backlog.title: Fresh base seed with full 200s budget

backlog.spec: In _optimize, accept a cap tuple argument. In the multistart loop, choose per restart from several schedules, for example (0.08,0.10,0.12,None), (0.10,None), (0.06,0.09,0.12,0.15,None), (0.12,None), (None,), using rng.integers. This diversifies which basins are reached while keeping the staged-growth idea that worked.
backlog.title: Randomized cap schedules per restart

backlog.spec: After the existing SLSQP polish, identify active constraints (pair gap < 1e-8, border gap < 1e-8) in the best packing. Solve the square or least-squares nonlinear system gap=0 for the active set over (x,y,r) with scipy.optimize.least_squares (xtol/ftol 1e-15) starting from the current solution, then accept only if _valid passes after a 1e-12 LP shrink and the sum increases.
backlog.title: Trust-constr active-set final polish

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that picks a row layout summing to 26 (for example 5,5,6,5,5 or 4,5,5,6,6 or 6,5,6,5,4, random permutation) and places circles evenly in each row with alternate-row offsets, jittered by sigma 0.02, with radii 0.07. Use it for 30% of the restarts, mixed with uniform random starts. Run through the unchanged staged SLSQP pipeline.
backlog.title: Hex-row structured starts with row-count variety

backlog.spec: Keep the top 3 distinct packings by LP score. For the last 60s of the budget, repeatedly pick one, delete 3 to 5 circles in a random disk region, re-seed those circles at random positions inside the disk with radius 0.03, and run the full staged _optimize. Accept if the sum improves. Region-local re-seeding differs from the random-circle perturbation tried earlier.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-relax from the top 3 with large moves

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, drop the circle with the smallest radius, and add a new circle in the largest empty hole (found by grid sampling the distance to the nearest circle edge). Then apply the staged SLSQP from that start. Repeat for each of the 5 smallest circles in turn. Accept the best result. This removes one specific circle rather than random ones.
backlog.title: Warm start from a rotated and reflected best packing with a dropped circle

backlog.spec: In the SLSQP stages, replace the objective -sum(r) by -sum(r^p) with p going 1.5, 1.2, then 1.0 across the stages, with analytic gradient p*r^(p-1). Convex-ish p>1 favors unequal sizes early, to push toward a few large circles, and the final stage returns to the true objective.
backlog.title: Weighted objective annealing of radius exponent

backlog.spec: Use random starts with SLSQP restricted to pairs whose initial center distance is below 0.5, which lowers the cost of each run by about 2x. Take the final solution of each, then rerun the uncapped stage with all pair constraints. This cuts per-start time and so increases the number of starts in the 200s window. Always finish with the full constraint set so validity holds.
backlog.title: Many cheap starts with a reduced pair-constraint set then full finish

backlog.spec: Draw the number of boundary circles nb uniformly from 12 to 16. Place nb circles along the square's perimeter at random sorted positions with a margin of 0.06 from the edge, and 4 of them at the corners if nb>=12. Fill the rest with uniform random centers in [0.2,0.8]. Use radii 0.06 on the boundary and 0.05 on the interior. Run through the staged SLSQP. Use this for every second restart.
backlog.title: Border-hugging ring plus random interior sampling with fixed circle counts

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP polish in construct_packing, identify active constraints (pair gaps r_i+r_j-d and border gaps below 1e-8). Solve the square or least-squares system of active equalities (d_ij = r_i+r_j, x-r=0 etc.) for z=(x,y,r) with a few Gauss-Newton/lstsq iterations to drive the residuals to ~1e-15. Then shrink radii by only 1e-13 and keep the result only if _valid passes and the sum is larger than the current best. This measures and reduces the margin cost.
backlog.title: Contact-graph rigidity Newton polish

backlog.spec: Replace the single default_rng(12345) multistart with four RNGs (seeds 7, 99, 2025, 31337). Run each for 45s, keeping the best per seed. Then fully polish each seed's best with the tight SLSQP _polish and return the best valid one. This differs from earlier splits because every seed's winner is polished, not only the global best.
backlog.title: Fresh base seed, 4-way time split with polish of each

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing. Remove the two smallest circles. Find the two largest empty holes by sampling a 200x200 grid and computing the distance to the nearest circle edge, using greedy selection with suppression. Place the circles there with radius 0.02, and run _optimize with the staged caps. Repeat for the 3rd to 6th smallest pairs, for 60s total. Accept only improvements in LP-scored sum.
backlog.title: Remove-two-and-reinsert at largest holes

backlog.spec: Add a search phase of 40s where the variables are 13 free centers and radii in a half-square, mirrored across x=0.5 (circles on the axis are self-mirrored). Use k axis circles from 2-4 and (26-k)/2 mirrored pairs, with k even. Optimize with SLSQP using the symmetric parameterization (z reduced, pair constraints computed on the expanded set). Then expand to the full 26 and run the unconstrained staged _optimize and _polish from it. Keep it if it is better.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric constrained search

backlog.spec: After the best packing is found, run a stage with an objective -sum(r)+mu*sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 + border violations^2) via L-BFGS-B with analytic gradient, with mu growing 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 from the best packing with random jitter of sigma 0.01 on the centers. After each run, repair with LP radii plus SLSQP. Run repeatedly for 60s, keeping any improvement.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant penalty annealing final stage

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for half of the restarts. Pick a row count pattern at random from the compositions of 26 into 5 or 6 rows with sizes 3-6 each, place the rows at evenly spaced y with a random stagger, and add jitter of 0.03 and radii of 0.05. Then run the usual _optimize and LP. Use a fixed new seed 4242 and a 200s guard.
backlog.title: Hex-row starts with variable row counts

backlog.spec: Generate starts where the radii are prescribed from the known good structure shape: 4 circles at 0.13, 8 at 0.10, 14 at 0.07. Place the large ones near the corners, and the rest uniformly at random with min distance rejection. Set r0 to the prescribed radii minus 20%, and use caps (0.10, 0.13, 0.16, None). Run for 100s then continue with the uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Corner-heavy size-prescribed starts with random assignment

backlog.spec: In _optimize, for the first two capped stages use only pair constraints with initial center distance below 0.45 (recomputed at each stage start), and use the full constraint set for the last two stages. This speeds up each restart by about 2x so more restarts fit in 200s. Keep everything else the same and use the freed time to run restarts with seed 8675309 after those of 12345.
backlog.title: Pair-constraint subset in early stages

backlog.spec: After the multistart, loop for 60s: pick a random center circle and its 5-8 nearest neighbors in the best packing, then rotate their centers about the cluster centroid by a random angle of 20-60 degrees, or reflect them. Shrink their radii by 50%, then run _optimize from this start with caps (0.12, None). Accept if the LP-scored sum improves.
backlog.title: Perturb incumbent by rotating a cluster

backlog.spec: In construct_packing change the rng seed from 12345 to 777 and keep everything else identical, but also record the best sum after each restart and, in the final selection, compare against the polished result. This samples a fresh basin set; the incumbent may be a lucky seed so a new stream may find a better optimum.
backlog.title: Multistart with 2-stage cheap-then-full using different base seed 777 and full 200s

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP polish, identify active contacts (pair gaps < 1e-8 and border gaps < 1e-8). Solve the square nonlinear system of active constraint equalities for x,y,r with scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'lm' or 'trf', xtol/ftol 1e-15) starting from the polished solution, using a minimum-norm step for underdetermined parts. Accept only if the LP-radii result with shrink 1e-12 is valid and larger than the current best.
backlog.title: Fixed-topology contact-graph Newton refinement

backlog.spec: In the final stage, instead of fixed shrinks 1e-12 and 1e-9, take the polished centers, solve the LP radii with shrink 0, then subtract the minimal amount per circle (start at 1e-15 and double until _valid passes) so the result is valid in double precision with the smallest possible loss. Return the largest valid sum.
backlog.title: Reduce shrink margin by exact verification loop

backlog.spec: For each restart, draw random centers, compute initial radii from _lp_radii on those centers (not a constant 0.05), then run the staged SLSQP from that feasible, locally-optimal radius vector. This gives each start an informed radii distribution rather than uniform 0.05.
backlog.title: Two-circle-class start: 4 big corners plus random with LP-radii-guided init

backlog.spec: After the multistart, run iterations: compute LP radii for current centers, take the LP dual values on the active pair constraints to form the gradient of sum r w.r.t. center positions (dual_ij * d(dist_ij)/dcenter), move centers by a backtracking line search along that gradient, and re-solve the LP. Run for 40s. This is a different first-order method on the nonsmooth max-sum function.
backlog.title: Alternating center-move and LP radius steps (LP-guided coordinate ascent)

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, apply one of the 8 square symmetries (irrelevant to the sum) and instead perform: delete the circle with the smallest radius and place it at a random location with radius 0.02 while shrinking neighbors by 10 percent, then run the staged SLSQP from caps 0.12 onward. Repeat with each of the 26 circles removed in turn (one per restart) within a 60s budget.
backlog.title: Rotated and reflected best packing with one circle dropped and re-added

backlog.spec: In _cons_fun add a margin parameter m so pair constraints require distance >= r_i + r_j + m and border constraints r <= x - m/2. Run stages with m = 0.01, 0.004, 0.0, which spreads circles out first and lets contacts form gradually. Make _cons_jac unaffected (the margin is constant). Apply across all multistart runs.
backlog.title: Anneal pair-constraint margin (inflated radii) during SLSQP stages

backlog.spec: Generate start centers by dart-throwing Poisson-disk sampling in the unit square with a minimum distance drawn per restart from uniform(0.14, 0.2), topping up with uniform random points if fewer than 26 are found. Use r0 = 0.05 and the existing staged SLSQP. This gives more evenly spread starts than uniform random.
backlog.title: Weighted random starts: Poisson-disk sampling with varied min distances

backlog.spec: After the multistart, loop until 215s: take the best centers, pick two circles of different radii whose centers are within 0.3 of each other and swap their radii only (keeping centers), add Gaussian jitter sigma 0.01 to all centers, set radii to 0.8 of the best, and run the full staged _optimize. Accept if the LP sum improves.
backlog.title: Perturbed-incumbent basin hopping with full staged SLSQP and radius swaps

backlog.spec: Generalize _N-dependent code to take n as a parameter (or temporarily set a module-level _N and indices). Run multistart SLSQP for n=27 for 40s, remove the smallest circle from the best result; separately run n=25 and add a circle in the largest hole. Use each as a warm start for the n=26 staged SLSQP and keep the best overall packing.
backlog.title: Mixed-n starting structure: optimize 25 or 27 circles then adapt

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop (stop it at ~120s), take the best packing and run repeated basin hops until 215s: pick 2-4 circles, swap the centers of a large and a small circle (or move one small circle to a random location), jitter all centers by sigma 0.01-0.03, set radii to 0.8x of the LP radii, then run the full staged _optimize (caps 0.12 and None only) and LP radii. Accept if the sum improves. Use a fixed rng seed. Keep the best and run the existing polish on it.
backlog.title: Incumbent-seeded perturbed SLSQP with radius swaps

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random starts in half of the multistart iterations with Poisson-disk (dart-throwing) samples of 26 points in [0.05,0.95]^2. Pick the minimum distance uniformly from 0.12 to 0.19 and retry until 26 points are placed (lower the distance by 5% on each failure). Use radii 0.5*min NN distance, clipped to the border distance. Feed these into the existing staged _optimize, alternating with the uniform starts.
backlog.title: Poisson-disk starts with varied minimum distance

backlog.spec: After the existing polish, find the active constraints in the best packing (pair gaps < 1e-9, border gaps < 1e-9). Solve the KKT system with scipy.optimize.least_squares on the active equations only (x-r=0 and so on, with (d-(ri+rj))=0 for the pairs). Use the minimum-norm Newton step from the current point, then exactly recompute the LP radii with shrink 1e-13. Accept only if _valid passes and the sum increases. This removes the SLSQP tolerance residue.
backlog.title: Fixed-topology contact-graph Newton refinement

backlog.spec: Run 30s of starts constrained to the diagonal mirror symmetry (x,y)->(y,x): 4 circles on the diagonal and 11 mirrored pairs, with a reduced variable set optimized by SLSQP with an analytic Jacobian by mapping the reduced variables to the full z. Then release the symmetry and run the full staged _optimize from the best 5 symmetric solutions. Keep the best overall.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric constrained search with free-orbit polish

backlog.spec: Add starts built from 5 rows with row counts chosen at random from permutations summing to 26 (e.g. 5,5,5,5,6; 4,6,4,6,6; 6,5,4,5,6). Place circles evenly within each row with half-spacing offsets between alternating rows, add Gaussian jitter of sigma 0.02, set radii to 0.07 and run staged _optimize. Spend 40s on these, then the remaining time on the existing uniform random starts.
backlog.title: Hex-row starts with row-count variety

backlog.spec: Add an extra SLSQP stage in _optimize before the final uncapped one, in which the pair constraints are relaxed to dist^2 >= (ri+rj)^2 - eps with eps annealed from 2e-3 to 0 over 3 sub-stages. This lets circles squeeze through narrow gaps. The final stage is the strict one, and LP radii then repair any residual overlap.
backlog.title: Overlap-tolerant final stage

backlog.spec: Run 1500 cheap starts, each with a single SLSQP stage (cap 0.10, maxiter 40) followed by the LP radii sum. Keep the top 10 distinct by sum, finish each with the full staged _optimize from the cheap result, and run the polish on the best. Use a 100s guard on the screening phase and spend the remaining time on random full starts.
backlog.title: Large-pool screening with LP score then finish top 10

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, repeat until 215s: pick a random circle in the best packing, select its 5-7 nearest neighbours, rotate their centers about the cluster centroid by a random angle of 20-90 degrees, shrink their radii by 30%, run the staged _optimize with caps (0.12, None) and LP radii. Accept if the sum improves. Use a fixed rng seed.
backlog.title: Perturb by rotating a local cluster

backlog.spec: On the best packing, alternate between two steps: (1) solve the LP for the radii, and take the LP dual values on the pair constraints; (2) move each center along the gradient of the dual-weighted sum of pair distances, with a line search on step size from 1e-3 to 1e-2, accepting a step only if the LP sum improves. Run until 60s are used or until no improvement. Then the final polish.
backlog.title: Coordinate ascent alternating LP radii and center steps

backlog.spec: In the staged SLSQP, replace the objective -sum(r) in the early capped stages with -sum(r^p) using p = 0.7 (which rewards many equal circles) in the cap-0.08 stage and p = 0.85 in the cap-0.10 stage, with the analytic gradient -p*r^(p-1) (clip r at 1e-6). The cap-0.12 and uncapped stages use p = 1. Use this for half the restarts and plain restarts for the other half.
backlog.title: Power-weighted sum with exponent annealing

backlog.spec: In construct_packing, cap SLSQP maxiter per stage at 150 for the first three capped stages (keep 300 for the final uncapped stage) so each start costs less, and raise the multistart time limit to 215s. This gives roughly 1.5-2x more starts within the same wall time. Keep the seed 12345, LP scoring and the final polish unchanged.
backlog.title: Time-boxed multistart with early-stop per-start budget

backlog.spec: During the multistart, store every result with LP sum above 2.62. After the loop, for the top 6, run alternating rounds (3 times) of: SLSQP polish with ftol 1e-15 from the current centers/radii, then LP radii re-solve on the new centers. Keep the best valid result. The shrink stays at 1e-12 with the _valid check.
backlog.title: Keep top-K diverse results and polish with LP-then-SLSQP loop

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing. For 40 trials: pick a random circle, delete it, find the point maximizing distance to the other circles and the borders by sampling 5000 random points, place the circle there with a small radius, then run the staged SLSQP (caps 0.12 and none) and LP. Keep improvements. Use a fixed rng seed and a 60s guard, and the multistart is reduced to 140s.
backlog.title: Incumbent-structure start with one circle relocated by hole search

backlog.spec: After the multistart, loop for 60s: take the best centers, add Gaussian noise with sigma drawn log-uniformly from 0.005 to 0.06 to all centers, and set radii to 0.7 times the best radii. Run only the uncapped SLSQP stage with maxiter 200, then LP. Accept if the sum improves. This is a basin-hopping variant with a log-uniform sigma sweep and a gentler radii start than earlier perturbation tests.
backlog.title: Anisotropic jitter of incumbent with tangent-pair preservation

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform start centers with a mixture. Draw each coordinate from uniform(0.05, 0.95), but with probability 0.4 per circle snap one coordinate to 0.08 or 0.92 plus noise of 0.02, so circles hug the borders. Keep r0 at 0.05 and the staged SLSQP. The 26-circle optima have many circles touching the border.
backlog.title: Edge-biased random starts

backlog.spec: In the final uncapped SLSQP stage only, add a quadratic term 1e-3*sum((r-rmean_local)**2) is not allowed; instead add a mild weighting objective -sum(w_i r_i) with w_i = 1 + 0.05*rand, redrawn per start, in the capped stages and then w=1 in the final stage. This perturbs which basin the staged growth chooses without changing the final objective.
backlog.title: Radius-sum objective with tiny contact-slack weights

backlog.spec: Vary the SLSQP ftol per start randomly among 1e-9, 1e-10, 1e-12 and maxiter among 150, 300, 500 in all stages. Early stopping at looser tolerances sometimes stays in different basins. Seeded from the same rng and the rest stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Run SLSQP in a rotated frame via constraint reformulation with tolerance sweep

backlog.spec: Generate starts by drawing 13 random centers in the left half (x in 0.05-0.5), mirroring them about x=0.5 with noise sigma 0.03 to give 26 centers. Run the staged SLSQP without symmetry constraints, then LP. Use for half of the starts, alternating with uniform starts. This is a soft mirror symmetry, unlike the earlier hard-symmetric tests.
backlog.title: Two-level start: random 13-center half packing reflected with noise

backlog.spec: Draw the initial radius r0 per start from uniform(0.02, 0.09), uniform across circles, instead of the fixed 0.05, and shuffle the cap schedule start between 0.07 and 0.09. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Larger early cap stage with variable r0

backlog.spec: After the final polish, instead of the global shrink 1e-12 then 1e-9, take the polished x, y and LP radii with shrink 0 and then subtract only the actual violation per constraint: for each circle, reduce its radius by max(0, max over pair and border violations, in double precision) plus 1e-16, iterating until _valid passes. Return it if it is valid and has a higher sum than the current output.
backlog.title: Final exact shrink minimization by per-circle bisection

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing. Run a loop (time guard 60s, seed 7): pick a random circle among the 6 smallest, remove it, and place it at the center of a random sample point among the 200 candidate points with the largest distance to the nearest remaining circle edge (largest holes). Also shrink its neighbors' radii by 10%. Run the full _optimize staged SLSQP from this warm start and keep the result if LP-scored sum improves. Final polish as before.
backlog.title: Incumbent-guided relocate with staged SLSQP

backlog.spec: Take the best multistart packing. Apply a random symmetry of the square (rotation/reflection) to a random half (circles with x<0.5), keep the other half, then remove overlaps by shrinking radii to 0.8x and repairing missing/duplicate circles by random reposition in the largest holes to get 26 circles. Run staged SLSQP from this and accept if better. Repeat for 40s with different seeds.
backlog.title: Reflect-and-drop warm start

backlog.spec: Add a start generator: choose 5 or 6 rows with random per-row counts (3-6) summing to 26, space rows evenly in y with margin 0.08, space each row's circles evenly in x with random offset, add jitter sigma 0.03, initial radii 0.07. Use this for 30% of multistart iterations, interleaved with uniform starts, using the same staged SLSQP.
backlog.title: Row-count hex starts with true variable rows

backlog.spec: Replace the final shrink choice with: compute LP radii with shrink 0, then for each circle subtract the smallest eps (found via bisection from 1e-15 to 1e-8) that makes the exact double-precision check (borders and pair distance sum) pass; keep the packing valid. This measures and minimizes the margin cost. Return the result.
backlog.title: Tight final shrink bisection

backlog.spec: After the multistart, run alternating steps: solve LP for radii given centers, read dual values of pair and border constraints, move the centers along the gradient of the LP value with respect to centers (sum of dual*d(distance)/d(center)) with a backtracking line search, step initial 0.01. Iterate up to 100 times or 60s and keep the improvement, then SLSQP polish.
backlog.title: Centers LP-dual gradient ascent

backlog.spec: For each multistart iteration, minimize -sum(w_i r_i) with w_i = 1 + 0.1*N(0,1) clipped to [0.8,1.2] for the first two capped SLSQP stages, and the true objective in the last two stages. This randomly biases which circles grow large, diversifying the basins. Implement by passing the weight vector into the objective and gradient.
backlog.title: Soft-start with radius-weight perturbation

backlog.spec: After multistart, for 80s: copy the best centers, swap the positions of a large circle and a small circle chosen at random, add gaussian jitter sigma 0.02 to all centers, set radii to 0.5 of LP radii, run staged SLSQP, accept if LP-score exceeds the best. Use seed 31.
backlog.title: Perturbed incumbent with large-small swaps

backlog.spec: Generate a start by sampling 13 random centers in x<0.5, mirroring them across x=0.5, adding gaussian noise sigma 0.02 to all 26 centers, initial radius 0.05. Use it for every third multistart iteration with the standard staged SLSQP (unconstrained symmetry).
backlog.title: Two-halves symmetric start with noise

backlog.spec: In _optimize, use per-circle radius caps: circles whose initial center lies within 0.15 of the border are capped at 0.10 in the first stages, interior circles at 0.14, while in the last stages everything is uncapped. Stages: (0.10/0.14), (0.12/0.16), uncapped, mapped per circle bounds.
backlog.title: Cap schedule on perimeter vs interior

backlog.spec: Keep the top 8 distinct LP-scored multistart results (distinct if sorted radii differ by more than 1e-3 in L1). Stop the multistart at 150s. For each, run 3 rounds of: jitter centers sigma 0.003, staged SLSQP uncapped only with maxiter 500, LP radii. Return the best valid.
backlog.title: Top-K diverse polish with jitter

backlog.spec: After the existing SLSQP polish in construct_packing, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-9 and border gaps < 1e-9) on the best packing. Solve the square system 'active gaps = 0' for x, y, r with scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'lm' or 'trf', xtol/ftol 1e-15), starting from the polished point. Then compute final radii by running _lp_radii with shrink=0, and subtract only the exact maximum violation, found by a loop that checks _valid on the result, instead of a flat 1e-7 or 1e-12. Keep the result only if _valid is true and the sum is larger than the current one. This measures and recovers the shrink-margin cost.
backlog.title: Contact-graph Newton polish with exact shrink

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, take the best packing and do a time-boxed (60s) loop. Each iteration: pick 2-3 random circles, translate each by a Gaussian step with sigma drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 0.15], and shrink their radii by 50%. Then run the staged SLSQP, with caps starting at 0.12 and then uncapped, warm-started from this point. Accept a result only if its LP-scored sum improves on the current best. Use a fixed rng seed.
backlog.title: Perturb incumbent with moves in tangent-graph null space

backlog.spec: From the best packing, drop the 3 smallest circles. Build a 25x25 grid of candidate points, compute for each the distance to the nearest remaining circle edge and border, and reinsert the 3 circles one at a time at the point with the largest free radius (take the max of the free-radius map, then update). Run the staged SLSQP from this start. Repeat with the 2-5 smallest circles and with randomly chosen circles. Accept improvements only. Run it for 60s, with a fixed seed.
backlog.title: Remove-k-circles and greedy reinsertion with SLSQP

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a square lattice with 5 columns, with random row counts 5-6. Give alternate rows a half-spacing offset. Assign a start radius of 0.12 to the 4 corner circles, 0.10 to circles on the edges and 0.07 to interior ones. Add Gaussian jitter of 0.02, then drop or add random points to reach exactly 26. Run the staged SLSQP. Alternate this with the uniform random starts in the multistart loop.
backlog.title: Two-scale mixed-size lattice starts

backlog.spec: In each multistart, set the SLSQP objective to -sum(w_i * r_i) with w_i = exp(0.3*N(0,1)). Linearly anneal the weights toward 1 across the four staged runs (w^(1-t) with t = 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1), so the final stage uses the true objective. This differs from slot 113, which perturbed weights only mildly and did not anneal them. It forces diverse size hierarchies that are not reachable from random centers.
backlog.title: Per-start lognormal radius objective weights with annealing to uniform

backlog.spec: Apply it to the top 5 packings kept from the loop. Repeat 200 times: solve the LP for the radii at the current centers, and read the dual variables of the pair and border constraints from linprog (res.ineqlin.marginals). Move each center by step*sum(dual*d(constraint rhs)/d(center)), where the pair distance gradient is the unit vector, and use a backtracking step size that accepts only LP sum improvements. Finish with an SLSQP polish. Time-box it to 40s.
backlog.title: Alternating LP-radii and center-gradient ascent

backlog.spec: Generate 13 random points in the left half and mirror them about x=0.5, which gives 26 circles with symmetric radii. Run staged SLSQP with the variable count halved (optimizing 13 centers and 13 radii, with the mirrored constraints built from the full set), then release the symmetry and run the full SLSQP from the symmetric optimum with a tiny random jitter of 1e-3. Do this for 60 seeds, since good packings of this kind are often nearly symmetric.
backlog.title: Soft-mirror symmetric packing with symmetry breaking release

backlog.spec: During each start, after the cap-0.10 stage, compute the LP sum. If it is below 2.45, abandon the start and skip the uncapped stages. Use the saved time for more starts, which lets the multistart cover roughly 2x as many starts within the same 200s budget. Make the threshold adaptive: use the 30th percentile of the stage-2 sums seen so far once there are 20 samples.
backlog.title: Time-boxed multistart with early abandon by LP bound

backlog.spec: In _optimize, use per-circle radius upper bounds in the staged runs. Circles whose start centers lie within 0.15 of the border get caps of (0.10, 0.13, none), and interior circles get caps of (0.07, 0.10, none), so that border circles grow first and the interior fills in later. Randomize the border and interior offsets per start by +-0.02. Keep the rest of the pipeline.
backlog.title: Cap schedule different for border vs interior circles

backlog.spec: In construct_packing, replace the uniform start with a two-class start: for each multistart draw k in 1..4 large circles (r0 uniform 0.12-0.16, centers uniformly random) and the rest small (r0 uniform 0.04-0.07). Keep the same staged SLSQP and LP pipeline and seed. Use it for every second start, alternating with the existing uniform start, so the existing behavior stays covered.
backlog.title: Mixed-radius-class random starts

backlog.spec: Final LP currently uses shrink 1e-7 inside the multistart scoring and 1e-12 only at the end. Change the multistart scoring to use shrink 0 in the LP (score only), so ranking is not biased. After picking the best, finalize with the smallest shrink in (1e-15,1e-13,1e-12,1e-10) that passes _valid. Report measured gain in a comment.
backlog.title: Lower margin via sum-aware shrink

backlog.spec: In _optimize, for the first two capped stages multiply the pair-constraint right side by a factor allowing 5% overlap: dx^2+dy^2 - (0.95*rs)^2 >= 0 (needs matching Jacobian scale 0.95^2 on the rs terms). Third and fourth stages use exact constraints. This lets circles pass through each other early to change topology. Fixed seed.
backlog.title: Slack-variable relaxed pair constraints early

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a 5x5 grid with spacing 0.2 (25 points) plus one extra point at a random location; apply per-point jitter sigma 0.04 and randomly delete/relocate 2-3 points to random positions. Set r0=0.07 for all. Run through existing staged SLSQP. Use for 30% of starts, rest uniform random with the same RNG.
backlog.title: Anisotropic square-lattice-with-defects starts

backlog.spec: Start generator: place 12 circles on the boundary at random perimeter positions (arc-length uniform, inset 0.08), 4 forced near corners, and the remaining 10 uniformly in [0.2,0.8]^2 with r0 0.08 on the border and 0.1 for interior. Use for half of the starts, alternating with uniform starts.
backlog.title: Optimize only top-border circle ordering via periodic boundary starts

backlog.spec: For the first two capped SLSQP stages use objective -sum(w_i r_i) with w_i = 1 + 0.3*(distance of center i from the square center)/0.707 (bigger weight for outer circles, pushing large corner/edge circles), then in the last two stages use w=1. Update _obj and _obj_grad to take weights via a module global set per start.
backlog.title: Radius-gradient-biased objective weights

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP, run up to 20 iterations of: solve LP radii for current centers, then compute LP dual multipliers for the pair/border constraints, and take a small center step along the gradient of sum of radii via dual-weighted contact normals (step 1e-3 with halving backtracking accepted only if the LP sum improves). Keep the best valid result. Budget 20 s.
backlog.title: Two-stage solver: SLSQP then active-set LP-Newton polish loop

backlog.spec: Stop the multistart at 120 s. Change the staged SLSQP maxiter to 150 for caps 0.08 and 0.10, and 500 for the final uncapped stage. Then take the top-3 distinct (by sum) packings and re-run the final uncapped stage with maxiter 1000 from each, picking the best. Tests whether under-converged final stages are hiding better basins.
backlog.title: Halved-time multistart with larger maxiter late stage

backlog.spec: Start generator: sample 13 centers in the left half [0,0.5]x[0,1] and mirror them across x=0.5 (with jitter sigma 0.01 so symmetry is soft). Run the cap 0.08 and 0.10 stages with the existing code and then the others as usual. Use for 25% of the starts; remaining starts are the existing uniform ones.
backlog.title: Symmetric-lite: reflect half packing then free release

backlog.spec: Build each start by sequentially adding circles: sample 200 random candidate points per circle, choose the one maximizing the min of distance to border and (distance to other centers minus their radii), assign r0 = 0.9 of that free radius, capped at 0.2. Repeat for 26 circles. Run staged SLSQP. Use for 30% of starts using the same seeded RNG, alternating with uniform starts.
backlog.title: Greedy sequential insertion starts

backlog.spec: Change the multistart loop so that SLSQP stage maxiter is 600 instead of 300 and ftol 1e-14 for every stage, keeping the 200s budget and seed 12345. Measures whether non-converged starts in the current loop are hiding better optima. Keep the final polish and validation unchanged.
backlog.title: Time-split across slow-and-deep vs many starts

backlog.spec: Inside _optimize, after the final uncapped SLSQP stage, apply a small Gaussian jitter (sigma 0.01) to the centers, set radii to 0.8 of the current radii, and re-run the uncapped SLSQP stage once. Keep whichever result gives the larger LP-radii sum. This is a cheap per-start local escape; applied to every start, using the same time budget.
backlog.title: Per-start perturbation of final stage then keep best

backlog.spec: Generate starts in which exactly k circles (k drawn uniformly from 10..16) are placed near the border (distance uniform 0.05-0.12 from a random edge, spread along the perimeter) and the other 26-k are uniform in [0.2,0.8]^2. Use r0=0.05. Replace 50% of the multistarts with these, alternating with the existing uniform starts. Differs from slot 48 by using a mixed interior and edge-distance jitter instead of fixed tangent ring.
backlog.title: Border-circle count conditioned starts

backlog.spec: For each start, first run SLSQP with only the 10 circles of largest starting-LP radius free (others' radii fixed at 0.03 by bounds and their centers fixed), then release all circles and run the existing staged schedule. Aim: lock in the big-circle skeleton before small ones fill gaps.
backlog.title: Larger-circle-first sequential SLSQP freezing

backlog.spec: Add a tiny term to the SLSQP objective, -sum(r) + 1e-3 * sum(r^2), during the capped stages only (analytic gradient 2e-3*r), and drop it for the last uncapped stage. This favors size-diverse configurations early, consistent with the best-known packings having mixed radii.
backlog.title: Lexicographic radius tie-break regularizer

backlog.spec: Run a short multistart (40s) for 27 circles using the same machinery (generalize _N via a parameter), then for each of the 27 circles in the best few results remove it, re-run the staged SLSQP for 26 circles from that warm start, and keep the best. Different from slot 79 by trying all single removals instead of only the smallest.
backlog.title: Incumbent-structure retargeting with n=27 removal

backlog.spec: Draw start centers uniform, then squeeze them toward a randomly chosen axis-aligned line or toward the center by a factor drawn from [0.6,1.0] on one axis, giving non-uniform density (clusters). Use r0=0.05. Apply to 30% of starts. Tests whether density-varied starts reach different basins.
backlog.title: Anisotropic scaling starts

backlog.spec: Reduce maxiter to 100 and ftol to 1e-8 on the first three capped stages, keeping 300 and 1e-12 on the final uncapped stage, so each start is cheaper and roughly twice as many starts fit in 200s. Keep everything else identical.
backlog.title: Lower-precision early stages with more restarts

backlog.spec: After the multistart, take the best packing, multiply all radii by 0.6, add Gaussian center noise sigma 0.02, then run the full staged SLSQP from it, repeated in a loop for 40s with sigma sampled log-uniformly in [0.005,0.05]. Accept if the LP sum improves. Differs from earlier perturb loops by starting with shrunk radii and rerunning the cap stages.
backlog.title: Warm-start from best with global scale-and-reshuffle of radii

backlog.spec: In the final uncapped stage, rebuild the constraint set to include only pairs with gap < 0.05 plus all border constraints, then re-run SLSQP from the result with the full set as a verification stage of maxiter 50. This gives faster, more precise convergence in the final stage and may escape slow-convergence stalls.
backlog.title: Sorted-pair constraint ordering and SLSQP with active-set reduction

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP polish in construct_packing, identify active constraints (pair gaps < 1e-9 and border gaps < 1e-9) on the best packing. Solve the square system of active equalities (pair distance = r_i+r_j, border tangency) for x, y, r using scipy.optimize.least_squares (method lm or trf, xtol/ftol 1e-15) starting at the current solution. Then shrink all radii by only 1e-13 plus the maximum violation measured in double precision, check with _valid, and accept only if the sum increases. Fall back to the existing result otherwise.
backlog.title: Tangent-graph Newton polish with exact shrink

backlog.spec: After the multistart loop, optimize a 27-circle packing with the same SLSQP stages for about 40s (the constraint code needs N as a parameter). Then for each of the 27 circles, drop it, run the staged SLSQP from the remaining 26 circles' centers and radii (all radii scaled by 0.95), LP-score the result, and keep the best if it beats the current best. This is a structurally different way to generate starts, not a perturbation of the incumbent.
backlog.title: Incumbent-seeded n=27 removal restarts

backlog.spec: Generate starts by sampling 13 random centers in the left half x<0.5, mirroring them about x=0.5 to give 26 circles, and adding noise of sigma 0.01. Run the first two capped SLSQP stages (cap 0.08, 0.10) with the mirror structure enforced by optimizing only the 13 free circles. Then release the symmetry and run the remaining stages on all 26 circles. Use this for 30% of the starts, with the rest staying uniform random.
backlog.title: Half-packing reflect start with free release

backlog.spec: Build each start sequentially. Keep a candidate grid of 40x40 points.
