Repeatedly place the next circle at the grid point with the largest free radius, meaning the minimum of the distance to the borders and (distance to each placed center minus that center's radius). Pick randomly among the top 5 points, and give the circle 0.9 of that free radius, floored at 0.02. After 26 circles, run the staged SLSQP from these centers and radii. Use for half of the multistart runs.
backlog.title: Greedy hole-insertion starts

backlog.spec: In _optimize, add a slack-inflation parameter. In the cap 0.08 stage, relax the pair constraints to dx^2+dy^2 >= ((r_i+r_j)*0.9)^2. In the cap 0.10 stage use 0.96, then 1.0 from the cap 0.12 stage onward. This lets circles pass through each other early and change topology. Keep the final stages exact, and LP-score as before.
backlog.title: Slack-relaxed pair constraints in early stages

backlog.spec: For each multistart, run only the cap 0.08 stage first (maxiter 100), then compute the LP sum for those centers. Continue the remaining stages only if the LP sum is above the 40th percentile of previous starts' LP sums at that stage, and otherwise abandon. Use the saved time to run about twice as many starts with the full 200s budget, and track the percentile with a running list.
backlog.title: Two-scale per-start time-split with early abandon

backlog.spec: After the multistart, loop for 80s. Pick a random circle in the best packing and its 4 to 6 nearest neighbors. Rotate their centers about the cluster centroid by a random angle in [-60, 60] degrees, or reflect them across a random axis. Shrink all radii by 0.7, run the final two SLSQP stages with uncapped radii, LP-score, and accept if better. Keep the best.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation perturbation of the incumbent

backlog.spec: In the final uncapped SLSQP stage, use objective -sum(r) - 0.002*sum(softmin-style penalty on small radii), computed as the -sum of exp(-r/0.02) with an analytic gradient. Then re-run the plain -sum(r) SLSQP from that result. The goal is to escape local optima in which tiny circles fill gaps, by first biasing toward balanced radii and then removing the bias.
backlog.title: Radius-regularized tail: lexicographic smallest-radius boost

backlog.spec: Draw k from 14..17 for the number of border circles. Place k centers on the perimeter at spacing near 2r with r0 about 0.07, including the 4 corners with r0 0.12. Place the remaining 26-k centers in the interior by Poisson-disk sampling with minimum distance 0.15, with r0 0.08. Run the staged SLSQP. Use for 40% of starts.
backlog.title: Border-count-constrained structured starts

backlog.spec: Run the first two capped stages in a stretched square: optimize on the rectangle [0,a]x[0,1/a] with a random aspect a in [0.9,1.1], with border constraints adapted. Then map the centers and radii back to the unit square by scaling the x coordinates by 1/a and the y coordinates by a. Reduce radii by the factor min(a,1/a), then run the final unit-square stages. This explores different topologies via a continuous deformation of the container.
backlog.title: Axis-stretched optimization coordinates

incumbent.description: After the multistart loop, re-polish the best packing with SLSQP (ftol 1e-15, maxiter 1000, near-active pairs only, gap < 0.02), then recompute radii with the LP at a 1e-12 shrink, falling back to 1e-9 if an explicit double-precision validity check fails, and keep the original packing if neither beats it.

memo:
Helped: replacing hand-placed rings with multi-start SLSQP (slot 0, -2.6118). Better starts followed: size-graded (slot 3, -2.6222), Lloyd-relaxed (slot 6, -2.6243), uniform random with fixed seed (slot 7, -2.6301). Staged radius-cap growth gave the incumbent (slot 8, -2.6360), past the 2.635 best known. Since then the loss has stayed at -2.6360 across dozens of runs. Slot 26's re-polish was accepted but gained nothing visible.
Did not help: perturb-best, basin hopping, populations, remove/reinsert, symmetric starts, penalty/barrier warm starts, DE, annealing, Powell/pattern search, multi-seed loops, finer caps (slot 36), Poisson-disk starts (slot 92). Worse: near-pair constraints (slot 4, -2.5957), screening starts (slots 51 and 53, -2.6296), ring start (slot 14, -2.6343), jittered grid (slot 21, -2.6353), contact reward (slot 35, -2.6307), margin annealing (slot 83, -0.5000).
Next: many slots were aborted as duplicates, so check the list first. The search is stuck at -2.6360. Try a structurally different approach, e.g. varying the circle count, and measure the shrink margin cost.
